🇲🇽🥇 <u>MEXICO SMASHES ALL-TIME GOLD RECORD AT CENTRAL AMERICAN GAMES</u>

Mexico just posted the best gold medal harvest in its Central American and Caribbean Games history: 152 golds in Santo Domingo, blowing past the previous record of 145 set in San Salvador.

With 346 total medals — 101 silver, 99 bronze — the delegation sits alone atop the medal table, just two medals short of the all-time total record. The record-breaking 146th gold came in modern pentathlon; distance runner Laura Galván closed out the 10,000m in 34:26.06. Regional hegemony, they call it. They're not wrong.

🇲🇽⚡ <u>CFE ELECTRIFIES MICHOACÁN: HISTORIC 99.99% COVERAGE</u>

The CFE completed 765 electrification works in Michoacán between January and July, pushing the state to a historic 99.99% electricity coverage — reaching communities across all 13 regions, many of them with solar systems.

Nationally, this administration has already built more than 17,000 electrification works — 300% more than the neoliberal governments that left remote villages in the dark for decades. Energy sovereignty isn't a slogan. It's a power line reaching the last town on the map.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>AYOTZINAPA: EX-GOVERNOR AGUIRRE ORDERED KEY VIDEOS DESTROYED — FGR</u>

For twelve years they said the videos didn't exist. They did — and former Guerrero governor Ángel Aguirre had them disappeared.

FGR chief Ernestina Godoy laid it out: cameras 12 and 15 outside Iguala's Palace of Justice recorded the Estrella de Oro bus carrying the 43 students as municipal and state police stopped it. The "technical failure" story was false. Two protected witnesses say Aguirre personally ordered the material destroyed in a meeting with his top officials.

"Far from an isolated act or technical omission, the concealment was a deliberate operation structured from the very top of the state executive." He faces forced disappearance charges. Where there was impunity, there is now investigation.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>MEXICO AND BRAZIL RELAUNCH BINATIONAL COMMISSION; LULA INVITES SHEINBAUM</u>

Latin America's two giants are back at the same table. Mexico and Brazil reconvened their Binational Commission — dormant for three years — with foreign ministers Roberto Velasco and Mauro Vieira agreeing on joint work in public health, agriculture, digital transformation, environment and space cooperation, plus Pemex-Petrobras collaboration.

Both governments also joined in backing Michelle Bachelet for UN Secretary General. Lula closed the day with a formal invitation for President Sheinbaum to make an official visit to Brazil.

🇲🇽⚒️ <u>US MINER NEWMONT BUSTED FOR UNION-BUSTING AT MEXICO'S BIGGEST GOLD MINE</u>

Mexico's Labor Secretariat (STPS) has officially confirmed that US mining giant Newmont violated freedom of association and collective bargaining rights at its Peñasquito gold mine in Zacatecas — the largest in the country.

The case was activated under the USMCA's Rapid Response Labor Mechanism after Newmont fired three local leaders of the National Miners Union. One worker was dismissed while running for secretary general of his union section — then named union delegate for the collective contract review anyway.

Under the T-MEC, labor rights are not a suggestion. Not even for US capital.
